newsitem.title: USA: Man convicted of horrific assault on pregnant woman.
newsitem.headline: Man convicted of horrific assault on pregnant woman.

text.p: A former New Mexico university instructor has been found guilty of kidnapping, sexually assaulting and attempting to murder an eight-months-pregnant student.
A jury of six men and six women deliberated for almost eight hours late Monday before convicting Eduardo Araiza, 26, on all seven counts against him. He faces up to 60 years in prison.

Araiza was arrested in March 1995 after luring Jennifer McBrayer, then aged 22, to his home to pick up an assignment near the New Mexico State University, where he was a graduate teaching assistant in English.

As McBrayer stood at the doorway of Araiza's home, he shocked her in the neck with a stun gun. He then handcuffed and gagged her before dragging her into a bathtub and cutting off her clothes with scissors.
A horrific, two-hour-long sexual assault followed.
McBrayer testified during the trial that she had pleaded with Araiza to let her go, at one point telling him she was having contractions and was about to give birth.
Araiza instead stuck a steak knife to her throat and held it there for several minutes, but then suddenly dropped the knife, helped McBrayer from the bathtub, removed her handcuffs and let her go.
McBrayer survived the attack and one month later gave birth to a healthy baby girl.
"It's over. The nightmare is over," McBrayer said in a telephone interview after Araiza's conviction.

Police searched Araiza's home after the attack and found two stun guns, a stash of pornographic videos and magazines, seven pairs of handcuffs and legcuffs and books about serial killers such as Ted Bundy and the Hillside Strangler.

Araiza, a struggling poet who portrayed himself as a bohemian on the university campus, confessed to the attack but pleaded temporary insanity. He told the jury he could not remember what happened and that he had been under intense pressure to complete his master's thesis.
The ashen-faced Araiza showed no emotion while two of his brothers wept on a back row of the courtroom when the guilty verdict was handed down.
"He took it like a man," Araiza's defence attorney Joe Edd Boaz said. "This was a no-win situation for Eduardo. He was either going to prison or a mental institution for the rest of his life."
A sentencing date has not yet been set.
